Why does coffee affect people in different ways?
a: Coffee affects different people in drastically different ways due to genetic, physiological, and lifestyle factors. The primary reason is genetic variation in the CYP1A2 enzyme, which is responsible for metabolizing caffeine in the liver. People with certain genetic variants of this enzyme metabolize caffeine quickly, experiencing shorter and less intense effects, while those with slower-metabolizing variants experience longer-lasting and more intense effects. Approximately 50% of people are 'slow metabolizers' who process caffeine more slowly, leading to higher peak caffeine levels and more pronounced effects like jitters, anxiety, and disrupted sleep. Fast metabolizers clear caffeine more quickly and may experience fewer side effects. Body weight and composition also play a role — smaller individuals tend to feel the effects of the same caffeine dose more intensely because the concentration per kilogram of body weight is higher. Tolerance is another major factor — regular coffee drinkers develop tolerance as their adenosine receptors become less responsive to caffeine blockade, requiring more caffeine to achieve the same stimulating effect. Hormonal fluctuations also influence caffeine sensitivity — women may experience different effects during different phases of their menstrual cycle, during pregnancy, or with hormone replacement therapy. Sleep deprivation amplifies caffeine's effects, making even small doses feel more potent. Age is another factor — older adults tend to be more sensitive to caffeine's effects due to slower metabolism and changes in body composition. Certain medical conditions, such as anxiety disorders, heart conditions, or acid reflux, can also affect how individuals respond to coffee. Additionally, the timing of consumption matters — caffeine consumed in the morning has different effects than the same dose consumed in the afternoon, due to natural circadian rhythms in alertness and hormone levels. The type of coffee and brewing method also influence caffeine content, with espresso containing more caffeine per volume than drip coffee. These individual differences explain why one person can drink coffee before bed without issue while another becomes jittery from a single cup.
